module: GE extension `core_vehicle_colors`: live changes of the color or paint of one of the 3 paint slots of the configured vehicle (core_vehicle_configTarget), updates the meshes through core_vehicle_manager.liveUpdateVehicleColors, then saves the paints in the config through core_vehicle_partmgmt.setConfigPaints (without respawn). Used by the vehicle configuration UI.
usage:
-- Full paint on slot 1 of the player's vehicle
core_vehicle_colors.setVehiclePaint(1, createVehiclePaint({x=0.8,y=0.1,z=0.1,w=1}, {0.5,0.5,0.8,0.1}))
-- Color from a string 'r g b a metallic roughness clearcoat clearcoatRoughness' (alpha from 0 to 2)
core_vehicle_colors.setVehicleColor(0, '0.8 0.1 0.1 2 0.5 0.5 0.8 0.1')
notes: setVehicleColor takes a JS index (0-based) whereas setVehiclePaint takes a Lua index (1-based).
colorStringToColorTable crashes the function (arithmetic on nil error) if the string contains fewer than 4 numbers.
The 4th component of the color string goes from 0 to 2; it is brought back to 0..1 by colorStringToColorTable then multiplied by 2 again in updateVehicleDataPaint before createVehiclePaint.

colorStringToColorTable.desc: Converts a string 'r g b a [...]' (numbers separated by spaces) into an array of numbers; the 4th element (0..2) is brought back to 0..1 (multiplied by 0.5 and clamped).

returns.desc: array of numbers; nil if colorString is nil

setVehicleColor.desc: Sets the color of a paint slot from a string (8 numbers: r g b a then 4 metallic values), updates the vehicle live and saves all paints in the config.

colorString.desc: 'r g b a metallic roughness clearcoat clearcoatRoughness'

objID.desc: vehicle; nil = configuration target or player 0

setVehiclePaint.desc: Applies a paint table to a slot, updates the vehicle live and saves the paints in the config.

objID.desc: vehicle; nil = configuration target or player 0

onVehicleSpawned.desc: Hook: a vehicle spawns. Copies its 3 actual colors (veh.color, colorPalette0, colorPalette1 + metallic data) into vehicleData.config.paints, rounded to 4 decimals, so that the config reflects the actual paint.
